notes: Latest year-over-year CPI rates are held constant as an explicit price scenario, not an official prediction or your measured personal inflation.
Only modeled variable spending changes with prices. Entered bills, rent, tuition, income and nominal goal targets stay at their saved amounts.
Broad spending categories use the all-items index when no closer series is available. Shopping is not assumed to be clothing.

Historical variable purchases are restated at the latest published category price level before training, then future price growth is applied. Holdout errors use those restated amounts, not a real-time CPI-vintage backtest.
Uses complete weeks and averages across all occurrences of each weekday, including zero-spend days. At least four complete weeks and three repeated occurrences are required for a prompt.
Groceries and routine purchases are kept separate. A bank transaction does not contain receipt items, shopping intent, or proof of an impulse purchase.
Mark a purchase as routine or planned to exclude it from habit prompts. It still counts toward spending and forecasts. Unreviewed transactions are not labeled discretionary.
Pending activity, foreign currencies and the current incomplete week are excluded. Posting dates can differ from the day you made a purchase.

frequency.note: Optional purchase counts, including zero-purchase days in complete weeks. After eight weeks and 30 purchases, weekday Poisson regression must beat a constant-rate baseline by 5% on the final 14 days. Imports may omit activity; rates are not calibrated risk probabilities.

payday.note: Optional daily spending on payday and the following two days, compared with the same weekdays one week earlier. This descriptive association can reflect plans, seasonality or income timing; it is not proof of a trigger.

research.title: Paycheck receipt and consumption timing
research.detail: Research motivates comparing days around pay. It does not show why a particular person spent money; scheduled payments can explain the pattern.

research.title: Payday and economic decision-making
research.detail: Findings on short-term scarcity and cognition are mixed. Surplus does not infer stress, self-control or a psychological condition.

research.title: Hawkes calibration and timestamp quality
research.detail: Clustering alone can mislead a self-exciting model. Surplus uses validated daily Poisson rates and descriptive sequences, not a causal impulse score.

notes: Times use genuine authorization timestamps converted to Toronto time; posting timestamps are never used to claim a two-hour purchase sequence. At least three distinct days are needed for a time-window or sequence observation.

Location summaries use city/region/country only, exclude online purchases and require three visits. No address, GPS, home/work inference or external geocoding is used. Missing location is not proof of an online purchase.
Recurring charge changes compare the first and last three observed charges, with monthly cadence and autocorrelation checks. They do not establish whether a service is unused or still active.

Merchant ticket trends compare median purchase amounts across two 90-day windows with at least four purchases each. Different basket sizes, tips and quantities prevent interpreting this as personal price inflation.
Personal set-aside estimates exclude reviewed loan and education reserves, unassigned cash, and future loan/grant deposits. Spending reduces personal cash first until you review the breakdown again.
Percentages count simulated paths, not calibrated overdraft probabilities. Historical daily bank balances and labeled low-balance events are not available to train a logistic or survival model.
This is combined CAD cash pressure after credit and pending reserves, not an account-specific overdraft prediction. A payment from one account can fail even if another holds money.

The optional set-aside amount protects the 10th percentile of each path's lowest balance over the whole forecast, your buffer, saved goals and all remaining goal targets. It is a one-time preview, never a daily transfer or a guarantee.
The five-day outflow rate is descriptive and includes bills. Detected pay dates are estimates. Confirm account balances and obligations before moving money.

weeklyPlan.note: Extra room is a one-time modeled margin beyond already projected spending, protecting the full forecast, buffer and goals. It is not a weekly allowance or guaranteed money.

accountOutlooks.note: Account estimates use observed variable outflows and assigned planned/detected payments. Unassigned payments, future transfers, variable pay and life-event adjustments are not allocated across accounts. Pending outflows are reserved. No account-specific risk probability is claimed.

assumptions: The band is the 10th to 90th percentile of 400 modeled paths, not a guaranteed or calibrated 80% confidence interval. Success rates describe these simulations only.

Variable spending uses a smoothed weekday profile when at least four complete weeks are available; otherwise it is spread evenly. Variable earnings are spread evenly. Posting dates and actual purchase dates can differ.

Published category CPI supplies a price scenario for variable spending. Fixed entered bills, income and nominal goal targets are not automatically inflated. The chart can compare constant future prices.
Current CAD cash is the starting balance. Credit balances, pending outflows, and existing goal savings are reserved. Investment and loan balances are not cash.
Monthly expense plans replace learned spending in their category. Tuition uses entered dates only. Other one-time expenses are additional future obligations.
Future confirmed funding and expected earned funding are included. Received money is already in the starting balance; applied or unconfirmed non-earned funding is excluded.

Saved earned funding or a confirmed work schedule replaces detected and learned employment income across the full outlook, even after a job ends. Gaps have no job pay unless another saved job covers them. Grants, loans, dated changes and what-if income remain separate.
Goals share one cash pool in priority/deadline order and protect the lowest remaining forecast balance through the horizon. Existing saved goal amounts must already be part of starting cash.

Personal savings estimates exclude loan, education-reserve and unassigned cash when a reviewed breakdown is supplied, plus future confirmed grant and loan deposits. Spending reduces personal cash first; review remaining funding after using education money. A what-if opening balance is unassigned.
Tuition readiness tests cash after the bill, buffer, and existing savings reserves. Its first cash coverage date can be temporary; check the deadline result as well.
A complete view requires all relevant accounts. Earliest observed activity does not prove uninterrupted coverage. An empty day in imported history is treated as no activity.
The what-if path adds your assumed extra income and reduces only modeled variable flexible spending. It changes no saved plan and makes no payments.
